entries.reason: a speed is a rate the release really has, and a name for it: the armv7 cache of 6.1.3 carries AVPlayer's `rate` (first rung 3.0) and `canPlayFastForward`/`canPlaySlowForward` (5.0), and not `defaultRate` (16.0). The port has no defaultRate to track, and says so in the row of selectedSpeed rather than inventing one
entries.effect: a speed answers the rate it was built with, the name it was given, and a numeric name derived from the rate in the device's own locale; +systemDefaultSpeeds answers the five the host answers, fastest first - 2 Double, 1.5 Faster, 1.25 Fast, 1 Normal, 0.5 Half - and those five names are the host's en_US strings, which is the open end of this row: no other locale's names are measured
entries.source: SDK 26.2 AVKit/AVPlaybackSpeed.h:26-67; the host's own AVKit, read by tests/backports/host/avkitspeeds at locale en_US@rg=plzzzz: 5 speeds, fastest first, and a speed built by the public initialiser named "port probe" at rate 1.75 answering the numeric name 1,75x, so that name is computed from the rate and not stored

entries.reason: the seam through which the 8.0 object's play path hands the play press to the 16.0 object that owns the speed: AVPlaybackSpeed.h:51 says the rate is set in response to the play button being pressed, and the press is handled in AVPlayerViewController.m, which must not define 16.0 API of its own
entries.effect: sets the player's rate to the selected speed's, and does nothing when no speed is selected or there is no player; the 8.0 object asks for it with respondsToSelector: first, because it also links in the bands that do not carry the 16.0 object
entries.source: no SDK header declares this name; the date is this port's own, the release whose object carries it, and it is defined in AVPlayerViewControllerSpeeds16.m and declared in CharonAVKitSpeeds.h
